rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide medical travel services in response to a worldwide medical event for NASA’s Human
Spaceflight Mission Directorate (HSMD), Johnson Space Center (JSC), or other travelers identified by NASA
(referred to as ‘traveler(s)’ throughout) on a pre-paid basis regardless of traveler’s home location or country of
origin.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide medical travel services worldwide for HSMD/JSC/NASA-identified travelers on a pre-paid basis regardless of location.

rows.verbatim: Provide transportation of patient from site of injury to appropriate medical facilities;
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide transportation of patient from injury site to appropriate medical facilities.

rows.verbatim: Coordinate with medical providers to ensure timely access to medical care;
rows.normalized: Contractor must coordinate with medical providers to ensure timely access to care.

rows.verbatim: Provide pharmacy assistance;
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide pharmacy assistance.

rows.verbatim: Obtain medical monitoring;
rows.normalized: Contractor must obtain medical monitoring.

rows.verbatim: Provide assistance obtaining medications, vaccines, blood transfers, and medical devices;
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide assistance obtaining medications, vaccines, blood transfers, and medical devices.

rows.verbatim: Obtain medical referrals and consultations with English-speaking doctors;
rows.normalized: Contractor must obtain medical referrals and consultations with English-speaking doctors.

rows.verbatim: Provide patient advocacy;
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide patient advocacy.

rows.verbatim: Provide bed side case management services such as in-person interaction and care;
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide bedside case management services including in-person interaction and care.

rows.verbatim:
Provide medical translation and interpretation services to include telephonic language assistance with medical
incidents and medical translations of medical records to the extent required to resolve the medical emergency;
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide medical translation/interpretation services, including telephonic language assistance and translation of medical records as needed to resolve the emergency.

rows.verbatim: Coordinate uninterrupted hospital admittance and discharge;
rows.normalized: Contractor must coordinate uninterrupted hospital admittance and discharge.

rows.verbatim:
Coordinate hospital payments including direct billing between insurer, medical provider and traveler, without
any involvement or responsibility of the Government;
rows.normalized: Contractor must coordinate hospital payments/direct billing between insurer, provider, and traveler without Government involvement.

rows.verbatim:
Coordinate insurance information between the patient, insurers, and medical providers, without any
involvement or responsibility of the Government;
rows.normalized: Contractor must coordinate insurance information between patient, insurers, and providers without Government involvement.

rows.verbatim:
Provide Guarantee of Payment (GOP) services and pay medical costs as an agent for the traveler to ensure
timely care and immediate discharge.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide Guarantee of Payment services and pay medical costs as the traveler's agent to ensure timely care and discharge.

rows.verbatim: Provide repatriation of mortal remains for travelers to the location specified by NASA;
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide repatriation of mortal remains to the location specified by NASA.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall transport the injured or ill traveler to nearest appropriate medical facility that practices U.S.
standards of medical care.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall transport injured/ill traveler to nearest appropriate medical facility practicing U.S. standards of care.

rows.verbatim:
In the event that the medical facility does not meet the U.S. standards of medical care, the Contractor shall
provide sufficient rationale to the NASA/JSC Chief Medical Officer and NASA Contracting Officer
Representative (COR) for using the proposed facility.
rows.normalized: If a medical facility does not meet U.S. standards of care, Contractor shall provide rationale to the NASA/JSC Chief Medical Officer and COR for using it.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall co-develop with NASA the notification process for timely communication, integration and
operational protocols with NASA physicians, and dissemination of confidential medical reports.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall co-develop with NASA the notification process for communication, integration/operational protocols with NASA physicians, and dissemination of confidential medical reports.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall obtain all necessary insurance information from the traveler, as required, and shall coordinate
the payment of personal medical expenses incurred by the traveler that are not arranged for or provided directly by
the Contractor.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall obtain necessary insurance information from the traveler and shall coordinate payment of personal medical expenses not arranged/provided by the Contractor.

rows.verbatim:
Such coordination shall be conducted exclusively between the Contractor, the traveler, and the
traveler’s insurer, without any involvement from the Government.
rows.normalized: Insurance expense coordination shall be conducted exclusively between Contractor, traveler, and traveler's insurer, without Government involvement.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide group membership as specified in Section B Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Group
Membership.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide group membership as specified in Section B FFP Group Membership.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor and the traveler will handle all subsequent GOP and pay as agent reimbursements directly between themselves.
rows.normalized: The Contractor and the traveler will handle all subsequent GOP and pay-as-agent reimbursements directly between themselves.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide transportation for three accompanying travelers specified by NASA on the same transport as the injured/ill individual requiring a medevac.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide transportation for three accompanying travelers designated by NASA on the same medevac transport.

rows.verbatim: In the event that the same transport cannot accommodate all three accompanying travelers, at least one accompanying traveler specified by NASA shall be accommodated on the same transport.
rows.normalized: If the transport cannot accommodate all three accompanying travelers, at least one designated traveler must be accommodated on the same transport.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide sufficient rationale to the NASA Contracting Officer Representative (COR) why it cannot transport all accompanying travelers and provide alternate transportation for the remaining accompanying travelers within 24 hours to the same location as the injured or ill traveler.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide rationale to the COR when it cannot transport all accompanying travelers and provide alternate transportation for remaining travelers within 24 hours.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor provided services shall meet the Commission on Accreditation Medical Transport Services (CAMTS), National Accreditation Alliance of Medical Transport Applications (NAAMTA) Global, and European Aero-Medical Institute (EURAMI) accreditation standards or equivalent for personnel and assets.
rows.normalized: Contractor's services must meet CAMTS, NAAMTA Global, and EURAMI accreditation standards or equivalent for personnel and assets.

rows.verbatim: Active credentials must be maintained according to the standard renewal timelines dictated by the respective accrediting body.
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain active credentials per the accrediting body's renewal timelines.

rows.verbatim: Any deviations must be reported to the JSC Chief Medical Officer and Contracting Officer Representative (COR), and approved by NASA prior to implementation, unless otherwise specified by the Contracting Officer.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report any accreditation deviations to the JSC Chief Medical Officer and COR and obtain NASA approval prior to implementation, unless otherwise specified by the CO.

rows.verbatim: The decision to perform a medevac shall be made jointly (50/50) by NASA and the Contractor, who will apply U.S. standards of medical care.
rows.normalized: The medevac decision must be made jointly (50/50) by NASA and the Contractor, applying U.S. standards of medical care.

rows.verbatim: This independent third party will be mutually agreed upon within 30 calendar days of contract award.
rows.normalized: An independent third party for evacuation disputes must be mutually agreed upon within 30 calendar days of contract award.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide a medical evacuation using a Portable Medical Isolation Unit (e.g. infectious disease) upon request by NASA.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide medevac using a Portable Medical Isolation Unit upon NASA's request.

rows.verbatim: If a medical event occurs, all costs for evacuation and additional medical travel services shall be the responsibility of the Contractor and no additional cost beyond the prepaid provided group membership as specified in Section B Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Group Membership amount will be incurred by NASA or its travelers.
rows.normalized: If a medical event occurs, all evacuation and additional medical travel costs are the Contractor's responsibility beyond the prepaid group membership amount.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall conduct a program status meeting each contract year with NASA management and JSC’s Chief Medical Officer, with the first meeting happening within 90 calendar days of the start of the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor must conduct a program status meeting each contract year, with the first meeting within 90 calendar days of contract start.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall participate in NASA Contingency Tabletop simulations of evacuation events to validate communication and operations plans and decision-making procedures (estimate twice per year).
rows.normalized: Contractor must participate in NASA Contingency Tabletop simulations of evacuation events.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide, within 60 calendar days of contract start and update annually for currency by Oct 1st, a Medical Facility Support Plan for each of the Russia and Kazakhstan medical facilities identified by NASA which contains the following:
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a Medical Facility Support Plan for Russia/Kazakhstan facilities within 60 calendar days of contract start and update it annually by Oct 1.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall establish and provide, within 60 calendar days of contract start and maintain for the duration of the contract, the GOP advance service agreements with the specific medical facilities that NASA identifies as critical medical facilities in Russia and Kazakhstan.
rows.normalized: Contractor must establish and maintain GOP advance service agreements with NASA-identified critical medical facilities in Russia/Kazakhstan within 60 calendar days of contract start.

rows.verbatim: If the Contractor cannot establish a GOP advance service agreement at one of NASA’s identified medical facilities in Russia/Kazakhstan by the end of that 60-day period, then the Contractor shall notify the NASA COR and provide an alternate course of action to meet the intent of the GOP advance service agreement.
rows.normalized: If the Contractor cannot establish a GOP agreement within the 60-day period, it must notify the COR and provide an alternate course of action.

rows.verbatim: Annually by December 15th, the Contractor shall provide a written summary report on the status of GOP advance service agreements for the NASA identified hospitals.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a written summary report on GOP agreement status annually by December 15.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall establish and provide, within 60 calendar days of contract start and updated annually for currency by Oct 1st, a written medevac plan of action/response for each location that NASA frequently visits to include Moscow, Russia; Baikonur, Kazakhstan; Karaganda, Kazakhstan; Nordwijk, Netherlands; Montreal, Canada; Tsukuba, Japan; and Tanegashima, Japan.
rows.normalized: Contractor must establish and provide a written medevac plan of action for each listed frequent-visit location within 60 calendar days of contract start, updated annually by Oct 1.

rows.verbatim: The plan shall include at a minimum:
rows.normalized: The medevac plan of action must include, at a minimum, the listed elements.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide a weekly report on current and historical NASA traveler enrollment and critical traveler information.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a weekly report on traveler enrollment and critical traveler information.

rows.verbatim: Travelers will not be required to be pre-enrolled or registered in a Contractor’s system in order for the Contractor to provide services covered under this contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor may not require travelers to be pre-enrolled/registered in its system in order to provide covered services.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide, by Sept 30th annually, a summary report of all medical incidents by date and incidence level (Levels 1-4), medical evacuations, reservations and call-ups of medical transport via air ambulance for Soyuz landings (if executed) supported by the Contractor during that year.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide, by Sept 30 annually, a summary report of medical incidents, evacuations, and Soyuz-related transport activity.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide, within 60 calendar days after contract award, wallet sized cards to the NASA COR for every NASA traveler with information including an international call number for support for medical support and emergencies.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide wallet-sized cards to the COR for every NASA traveler within 60 calendar days after contract award.

rows.verbatim: Approximately 1,200 cards are required annually for NASA travelers.
rows.normalized: Approximately 1,200 wallet cards are required annually for NASA travelers.

rows.verbatim: The cards shall be updated for currency and provided annually thereafter to the NASA COR by Oct 1st.
rows.normalized: Contractor must update and provide the wallet cards annually thereafter to the COR by Oct 1.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide a Reservation and Call-up/Execution service for medical transport via air ambulance for Soyuz crew landing event.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a Reservation and Call-up/Execution service for Soyuz crew landing medevac transport.

rows.verbatim: Within 36 hours of NASA reservation, the Contractor shall provide a Reservation Readiness Package consisting of a dedicated tail-number assignment, overflight and landing permits, diplomatic route clearances, aircraft medical and transport capabilities, and staffing plan.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a Reservation Readiness Package within 36 hours of NASA's reservation.

rows.verbatim: NASA will provide call-up/execute notification to the Contractor no later than 36 hours prior to the Soyuz landing event.
rows.normalized: NASA will notify the Contractor for call-up/execution no later than 36 hours prior to Soyuz landing, triggering the Contractor's response obligations.

rows.verbatim: The crew member and the associated NASA flight surgeon shall be transported to Houston, Texas.
rows.normalized: The crew member and NASA flight surgeon must be transported to Houston, Texas.

rows.verbatim: Within 3 hours of the NASA call-up, the Contractor shall activate the asset and personnel and provide an Operational Deployment Package consisting of a copy of the officially filed International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) flight plan, crew-rest compliance, real-time satellite tracking link, confirmation of NASA passengers on flight manifest, finalized staffing plan, and communications matrix.
rows.normalized: Contractor must activate assets/personnel and provide an Operational Deployment Package within 3 hours of NASA's call-up.

rows.verbatim: If a reservation or call-up for medical transport via air ambulance occurs, all costs for the reservation and medical transport via air ambulance shall be the responsibility of the Contractor and no additional cost beyond the prepaid reservation fee and call-up fee as specified in Section B Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Group Membership amount will be incurred by NASA or its travelers.
rows.normalized: If a reservation or call-up occurs, all related transport costs are the Contractor's responsibility beyond the prepaid fees.

As this procurement will result in a firm-fixed-price purchase order, Offerors shall provide firm-fixed pricing that is all-
inclusive (including profit and fees) for the required services on the within Section B – Supplies or Services & Prices above.
rows.normalized: Because the award will be firm-fixed-price, Offerors shall provide all-inclusive firm-fixed pricing in Section B.

rows.verbatim: Additional pricing terms will not be accepted.
rows.normalized: Additional pricing terms submitted by offeror will not be accepted.

rows.verbatim:
The Offeror shall submit a completed Proposal Pricing within Section B - Supplies or Services & Prices above with their
proposal.
rows.normalized: Offeror shall submit a completed Section B Proposal Pricing with its proposal.

rows.verbatim: If the Government orders Medevac Using Portable Medical Isolation Unit (e.g. infectious disease) coverage for the stated periods, the sum of tables “a” and “b” shall represent the total price of services.
rows.normalized: If the Government orders Medevac Using Portable Medical Isolation Unit coverage for the stated periods, the total price of services must equal the sum of tables 'a' and 'b'.
